marble.name: Fractions on a number line
marble.subject: Mathematics
marble.description: Recognise and use fractions as numbers: place unit fractions and non-unit fractions with small denominators on a number line
marble.prompt: If you draw a number line from 0 to 1, can you mark where 1/4, 1/2, and 3/4 should go — without any extra help?

cluster.summary: Your child is discovering their first fractions — learning to recognise and name halves and quarters as equal parts of shapes, objects, and groups.

misconceptions: Treats the number line like a ruler — counts tick marks (or draws 4 marks for fourths) instead of equal segments (IES Roadblock 2.1)
Places 3/4 between 3 and 4, treating numerator and denominator as separate whole numbers (IES Roadblock 2.2)
Treats the whole line as the unit — e.g. locates 3/4 three-quarters of the way across a 0-to-5 line
Sees a fraction only as part of a shape, not as a single number that has a place on a line
representations: 0-to-1 number line partitioned into equal segments (the core model)
Dual-labelled line (two fractional-unit sequences) for equivalence
Fraction strip laid alongside the line to link area-model and length-model
authoredAnswer: The dot is at 3/4, because 0-to-1 is divided into four equal parts (segments) and the dot sits at the end of the third part. On the 0-to-4 line, 3/4 goes three-quarters of the way from 0 towards 1 (just below 1, NOT between 3 and 4) and 1/2 goes halfway between 0 and 1; each is a single number between 0 and 1 because its denominator splits ONE unit.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Reads the 3/4 point as 4/4 or 4/5, counts the 0 mark as one, or when drawing puts four interior marks to make fourths
wrongAnswers.fix: Show fourths as four equal SEGMENTS made by THREE marks between 0 and 1; have the child colour each segment and count segments, not marks (IES Roadblock 2.1)

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: On the 0-to-4 line marks 3/4 in the interval from 3 to 4
wrongAnswers.fix: Contrasting cases: locate 3 and 4, then 3/4 as a number between 0 and 1; reteach fraction as a single quantity of one whole before returning to the line (IES Roadblock 2.2)

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Refuses the task, treats the line as decoration, or places the fraction with no relation to the unit
wrongAnswers.fix: Bridge the area model to length: lay a fraction strip along the 0-1 line so the shaded part reaches the same point; name the point as the number

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: When asked to place unit fractions, puts the one with the bigger denominator further to the right
wrongAnswers.fix: Partition the same unit into thirds then eighths and compare segment lengths; reteach more-parts-means-smaller before ordering on the line
